analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date, adds documentation of GLM5Next logprobs tests (GLM5NextLogprobsTests, SDK GLM5NextMTPTests logprob cases, NativeOutputControlRefusalTests), and adds OpenRouter-compat test documentation (GLM5NextOpenRouterCapabilityTests, reasoning-content return tests, captured strict weather-tool requests, JSON response_format/forced tool_choice validation and content-free 422 behavior). I examined the base units (lines 489-1098) and the head unit (lines 1-482) and found no code, configuration, key-handling, authorization, attestation, or cache-storage behavior changed. The documented tests use tiny local fixtures, scripted engines and synthetic credentials, with no production endpoints.

Threat-model relevance: the docs mention a logprobs relay channel and 'content-free 422' failure behavior, which touches A-001 (prompt/completion confidentiality) only as a test description. No T-041 cache mechanics (TTL, HMAC lookup tags, KEK, AAD, cache gating) are altered in the visible text, and no new env flags affect security posture beyond test-only gating. Caveat: the patch excerpt and head text are truncated (head unit shows only lines 1-482 and the patch excerpt is incomplete), so any later head-side changes in lines 483-end are not visible. The visible range map says head changes are at 3, 117-126 and 182-208, which I covered. The documented provider/SDK behavior, such as logprobs emission via the coordinator relay and whether logprobs leak reasoning that should be withheld, is implemented in unsupplied source and should be reviewed there. This PR itself introduces no concrete security regression.
